clue.text: Notice one left on the railway?

definitions.text: Notice one left on the railway?

parts.note: a notice is a sign put up to inform people
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a notice has been abandoned beside the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a railway signal is a notice set beside the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway signal is a lineside indicator that tells drivers whether they may proceed, a notice on the track.

clue.text: Does it show the way to endorse letters?

definitions.text: Does it show the way to endorse letters?

parts.note: to endorse a cheque or document is to sign it
letters delivered are the post or mail

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether signing mail points out a route.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening question defines the answer while the rest builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingerpost at a junction directs travellers, so it shows the way.

clue.text: Large company at Ulster?

parts.note: large means great

explanation.surface: A question about some big firm based in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the Irish province, but an ulster is also a long, heavy overcoat, named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a heavy belted overcoat of the kind soldiers wore, an example of this garment.

clue.text: Get off in one respect

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
in one respect means in one way, so respect gives way

explanation.surface: Dismount, in a certain sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off!' is an order to leave, the same exclamation as 'Away!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commands telling someone to leave at once, as in 'away with you'.

clue.text: Fool was indisposed but attacked

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to be indisposed is to be ill, so 'was indisposed' means ailed

explanation.surface: A foolish person was unwell yet came under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being assailed means being set upon violently, the same as being attacked.

clue.text: Curse about note from jumper-

indicators.note: about means going around, so the curse word encloses the note

parts.note: to curse is to swear
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone swears over a message left by a person who jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like someone who leaps; in Britain it is the word for a knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a jumper is a knitted pullover, the garment Americans would also call a pullover top.

clue.text: Apply to receive a revenue ostensibly

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: rent is income or revenue from property

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply in order to collect some income, seemingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' reads as plain instruction, but it tells the first word to take the following pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensibly means seemingly, on the face of things, which matches the adverb.

clue.text: Incumbent could be untruthful

definitions.meaning: incumbent in its old sense means resting or reclining on something

explanation.surface: An office-holder might be a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incumbent' suggests an office-holder, but here it has its literal sense of lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent or reclining is one sense; telling falsehoods is the other, both covered by the same participle.

clue.text: Died on land in famine

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the next piece follows

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
earth is ground or land

explanation.surface: Someone perished on the soil during a famine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, especially of food, so a famine.

clue.text: Can that is right but smaller

parts.note: a can is a tin
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A tin can is fine, but a lesser size.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinier is the comparative of tiny, meaning more small.

clue.text: Missile taking in syrup

indicators.note: taking means taking inside, so the missile encloses the next word

parts.note: a grenade is a thrown explosive missile
in is taken as written

explanation.surface: A projectile absorbing a sweet liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a red pomegranate cordial used in cocktails, a kind of sweet syrup.

clue.text: The first formal one

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The opening formal item.
explanation.walkthrough: Prima is Italian for first, as in prima donna and prima ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima is the Italian feminine word for first, as in the leading lady of an opera company.

clue.text: The innermost part of mine with gas

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: The deepest part of a coal mine filled with gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith is the soft inner tissue of a stem, and figuratively the core or essence.

clue.text: Beginning to put in order a -privilege to which all are entitled

definitions.text: privilege to which all are entitled

parts.note: birth is a beginning
to right something is to put it straight or in order

explanation.surface: A starting point: put in order a privilege everyone has.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is an entitlement one holds from the moment of being born.

clue.text: Minister with an opportunity to turn up

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A government minister given a chance to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROLL into LLOR. In Britain the Chancellor of the Exchequer is the finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the British cabinet minister in charge of finance.

clue.text: Conceal southern dam

parts.note: a dam is an animal mother

explanation.surface: Hide the reservoir wall in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' suggests a barrier on a river, but it is the word for an animal's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up and suppress it, so to conceal it.

clue.text: Cause festering in right joint

parts.note: the ankle is a joint

explanation.surface: An infection festering in the right-hand joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle originally meant for a wound to fester, and now for a grievance to continue to irritate.

clue.text: Fast and flashy and not without a 'peal

definitions.text: Fast and flashy and not without a 'peal

parts.words: Fast and flashy and not without a 'peal
parts.note: something very quick and bright as a flash, and usually accompanied by a peal of thunder

explanation.surface: Something quick and showy, with a certain appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peal hints at appeal, but it is a peal of thunder. The answer is proverbially fast, it flashes, and thunder follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical discharges in a storm are proverbially fast, appear as flashes and come with thunderclaps.

clue.text: One left right in the light should-be…

definitions.text: One left right in the light should-be…

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes into the next word

parts.note: light is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in the illumination ought to be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside LIGHT after its L. The answer completes the clue's unfinished sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fine or satisfactory is what 'should be' expects; the phrase means safe and well.

clue.text: Being *drunk, throw bricks

definitions.meaning: being very drunk or high, a slang sense
having had stones or bricks thrown at one

explanation.surface: While intoxicated, someone hurls masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, and also the past participle of pelting with rocks.

clue.text: Furniture that is useful backstage

definitions.meaning: a sideboard with shelves for dishes
a theatre assistant who helps actors into costume

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture handy behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cupboard with shelves, and a theatre helper who looks after actors' costumes.

clue.text: Sick eastern convict returning against the law

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for convict is read backwards

parts.note: lag is British slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: An unwell eastern prisoner coming back breaks the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LAG into GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illegal is unlawful, forbidden by statute.

clue.text: An encroachment but it could be no raid

indicators.note: could be means the letters may become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An intrusion that perhaps was not an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NO RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance into someone else's territory, an encroachment.

clue.text: Selfishness, for example, is in order

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word is goes into the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Self-interest is acceptable, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like 'tidy', but the order is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is the habit of putting one's own interests first, so self-centredness.

clue.text: Bird served with fruit, not wanted by lovers

parts.note: a goose is a bird
a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A goose dish served with fruit, which courting couples dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain to 'play gooseberry' is to be the unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom calls the unwelcome third party tagging along with a courting couple by this name.

clue.text: Begins with duck and other birds

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, written O
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: It starts with a duck and some other birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a nil score in cricket, shaped like a duck's egg; pens are female swans.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to start it, so opens means commences.

clue.text: A guide for sailor from the south

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Navigation for a seaman coming from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors once steered by the stars, which is why one makes a fitting guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafarers navigated by the stars, so one in the sky serves as a guide.

clue.text: Game in which of 29 may be called

definitions.text: Game in which of 29 may be called

parts.words: Game in which of 29 may be called
parts.note: a card game in which a bid named from the first part of the psalm at 29 may be declared

explanation.surface: A card game in which part of a psalm may be called out.
explanation.walkthrough: In solo whist a player may bid misère, undertaking to win no tricks; misère is the first part of 29's MISERERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game where misère is one of the bids declared.

clue.text: One business transaction is excellent

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A single business transaction proves first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect or most suitable, so excellent.

clue.text: Main song taking in added flavour

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea

indicators.note: taking means taking inside, so the song encloses the next word

parts.note: in is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea shanty soaking up extra taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal', but the main is the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoning is the salt, pepper or herbs added to food for flavour.

clue.text: Psalm sung before following niggard

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for before is placed after the miser

parts.note: a niggard is a miser
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A psalm performed in front of a stingy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The Miserere is Psalm 51 (50 in the Vulgate), from its Latin opening 'Miserere mei'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miserere is Psalm 51, named from its Latin opening words, often set to music.

clue.text: Neglect to fabricate a type of shirt

parts.note: to forge is to fabricate or fake
a T-shirt is a type of shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: Neglect to make a fake kind of shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget a duty is to fail to attend to it, so to neglect it.
